control_flow.reason: For successfully parsed objects, the entry reaches json_unpack, which initializes its scanner and dispatches the fixed formats. This foundation does not make the keyed array route reachable.

json_vunpack_ex dispatches unpack and cleans up its copied argument list.

blockers.requirement: Within object-member unpacking, a format expecting an array must be reachable with a wrong-type member so the supported array diagnostic can include that member's key.
blockers.target_route: A finite input consisting of a selector byte followed by {"data":42} parses as an object. A member-array format would make unpack_object look up data, pass its key to unpack, and dispatch '[' to unpack_array's wrong-type guard.
blockers.failure_condition: The old entry instead calls "{s?o}" for object members; o accepts the integer. Its only array format, "[o!]", is called only when the root is already an array, and top-level unpack starts with a null parent key. The entry also calls json_unpack without an error object, so it cannot expose diagnostic text.
blockers.alternative_paths: The root "o" call only returns the object. Changing JSON bytes cannot change either fixed format or the root-array guard; deep copy and dump do not invoke unpack_array.
